skill.name: legacy-modernizer
skill.description: Refactor legacy codebases, migrate outdated frameworks, and implement gradual modernization. Handles technical debt, dependency updates, and backward compatibility. Use PROACTIVELY for legacy system updates, framework migrations, or technical debt reduction.
skill.summary: Plan safe, incremental modernization for legacy codebases while preserving existing behavior.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Legacy systems are hard to change without breaking users or integrations. This skill guides incremental upgrades, compatibility planning, tests, and rollback paths.
actual_capabilities: Creates phased migration plans with milestones and rollback steps.
Recommends tests that protect existing legacy behavior before refactoring.
Plans framework, language, dependency, and database modernization work.
Designs adapter layers, compatibility shims, and API versioning strategies.
Identifies rollout controls such as feature flags and deprecation timelines.
limitations: It is a prompt-only skill and does not run migrations by itself.
It needs project context, constraints, and risk tolerance from the user.
It cannot guarantee compatibility without repository tests and production validation.
It focuses on modernization planning, not unrelated product or design work.

use_cases.title: Plan a Framework Migration
use_cases.description: Create a phased path from an outdated framework to a supported framework while preserving user-facing behavior.

use_cases.title: Reduce Technical Debt
use_cases.description: Prioritize risky legacy modules, add tests, and schedule refactors that reduce maintenance cost.

use_cases.title: Design a Safe Rollout
use_cases.description: Define compatibility shims, feature flags, deprecation notices, and rollback criteria for a modernization release.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Legacy Risk
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner assessment for an unfamiliar codebase.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this legacy system context and identify the highest modernization risks. Suggest a safe first phase with tests and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create Migration Phases
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a known upgrade target.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a phased migration plan from the current stack to the target stack. Include milestones, dependencies, owners, and rollback criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Protect Existing Behavior
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced refactoring preparation before code changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a test strategy for this legacy module before refactoring. Cover critical paths, integration boundaries, fixtures, and regression checks.

prompt_templates.title: Modernize With Compatibility
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced modernization across APIs or services.
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose a compatibility architecture for this migration. Include adapters, API versioning, feature flags, deprecation timing, and operational safeguards.

output_examples.input: Migrate a Java 8 service to Java 17 without disrupting clients.
output: Inventory dependencies and runtime constraints before changing language level.
Add regression tests around public APIs and batch jobs.
Upgrade build tooling in a separate phase from framework changes.
Release behind staged deployment gates with rollback instructions.

output_examples.input: Reduce risk in a legacy monolith before splitting services.
output: Map module ownership, data boundaries, and shared database writes.
Add characterization tests around high-change workflows.
Extract one bounded capability behind an adapter first.
Track latency, error rates, and rollback triggers during rollout.

best_practices: Add tests around current behavior before changing implementation details.
Use incremental releases with feature flags and measurable rollback criteria.
Document breaking changes, deprecation windows, and integration impacts.
anti_patterns: Rewriting an entire system without a migration path.
Upgrading dependencies and architecture in the same untested release.
Removing compatibility layers before downstream users have migrated.

faq.question: What kind of legacy work does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports framework migrations, dependency updates, refactoring plans, database modernization, and compatibility strategies.

faq.question: Can it modernize code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides plans, checklists, and implementation guidance for an AI coding assistant or developer.

faq.question: Does it require test coverage first?
faq.answer: It strongly recommends tests before refactoring because tests protect existing behavior during modernization.

faq.question: Can it help with monolith decomposition?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan gradual service extraction, module boundaries, adapters, and rollout controls.

faq.question: How does it handle backward compatibility?
faq.answer: It recommends adapter layers, API versioning, deprecation timelines, and staged rollout safeguards.

faq.question: Is it suitable for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
